lesson_scope: Equilibrium of particles on smooth inclined planes; resolution of weight into components parallel and perpendicular to the line of greatest slope; holding forces parallel to the plane, horizontal, and inclined at general angles; normal contact force without friction; connected particles across smooth pulleys at the crest of inclines; double-faced triangular wedges; and lift-off contact loss thresholds.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Weight components parallel and perpendicular to inclined plane

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Weight components parallel and perpendicular to inclined plane

hints: The weight vector acts vertically downwards. Down the slope, the component is $mg\sin\theta = 50\sin 30^\circ = 25\text{ N}$.
Perpendicular to the slope, the component is $mg\cos\theta = 50\cos 30^\circ = 25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the component of weight acting down the line of greatest slope:
$$W_\parallel = mg\sin 30^\circ = 5(10)(0.5) = 25\text{ N}$$

Calculate the component of weight pressing perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$W_\perp = mg\cos 30^\circ = 5(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3013 \approx 43.3\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Resolve gravity along the slope:
- Downward sliding tendency:
$$W_\parallel = 50\sin 30^\circ = 25\text{ N}$$

Resolve gravity into the slope:
- Contact pressing force:
$$W_\perp = 50\cos 30^\circ = 25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates parallel component down the plane: $W_\parallel = mg\sin 30^\circ = 50(0.5) = 25\text{ N}$.
Calculates perpendicular component into the plane: $W_\perp = mg\cos 30^\circ = 50\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 2: Holding force parallel to the slope and normal reaction

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Holding force parallel to the slope and normal reaction

hints: Because the plane is smooth, there is no friction. The holding force $P$ directly balances the component of weight down the slope: $P = mg\sin 30^\circ = 30\text{ N}$.
The normal reaction balances the perpendicular weight component: $R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 30\sqrt{3} \approx 52.0\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_\parallel = P - mg\sin 30^\circ = 0$$
$$P = 6(10)(0.5) = 30\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_\perp = R - mg\cos 30^\circ = 0$$
$$R = 6(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 30\sqrt{3} \approx 51.9615 \approx 52.0\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Balance along the smooth slope:
- With no friction, the uphill force must equal the downhill pull of gravity:
$$P = mg\sin 30^\circ = 60 \times 0.5 = 30\text{ N}$$

Balance perpendicular to the slope:
- The plane pushes back against the perpendicular weight:
$$R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 30\sqrt{3} \approx 52.0\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves parallel to the slope: $P = mg\sin 30^\circ = 60(0.5) = 30\text{ N}$.
Resolves perpendicular to the slope: $R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 60\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 30\sqrt{3} \approx 52.0\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 3: Horizontal holding force on a smooth inclined plane

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Horizontal holding force on a smooth inclined plane

hints: A horizontal force makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with the line of greatest slope, so its component up the slope is $P\cos 45^\circ$.
Equate components along the slope: $P\cos 45^\circ = mg\sin 45^\circ \implies P = mg\frac{\sin 45^\circ}{\cos 45^\circ} = mg\tan 45^\circ = 4(10)(1) = 40\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up equilibrium along the line of greatest slope:
$$\Sigma F_\parallel = P\cos 45^\circ - mg\sin 45^\circ = 0$$
$$P\cos 45^\circ = 4(10)\sin 45^\circ$$

Solve for the horizontal force $P$:
$$P = 40\left(\frac{\sin 45^\circ}{\cos 45^\circ}\right) = 40\tan 45^\circ = 40(1) = 40\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Resolve the horizontal push along the slope:
- The uphill push component is $P\cos 45^\circ$:
$$P\cos 45^\circ = mg\sin 45^\circ$$

Solve for $P$:
- Since $\tan 45^\circ = 1$, the push equals the weight:
$$P = 40\tan 45^\circ = 40\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves along the inclined plane: $P\cos 45^\circ = mg\sin 45^\circ$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Normal reaction under horizontal pushing force

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Normal reaction under horizontal pushing force

hints: Notice that the horizontal force $P$ pushes into the slope, so its component perpendicular to the slope adds to the perpendicular weight component.
Resolve perpendicular to slope: $R = mg\cos 45^\circ + P\sin 45^\circ = 40\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) + 40\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 40\sqrt{2} \approx 56.6\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_\perp = R - mg\cos 45^\circ - P\sin 45^\circ = 0$$
$$R = mg\cos 45^\circ + P\sin 45^\circ$$

Substitute $mg = 40\text{ N}$ and $P = 40\text{ N}$:
$$R = 40\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) + 40\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 20\sqrt{2} + 20\sqrt{2} = 40\sqrt{2} \approx 56.5685 \approx 56.6\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Sum the perpendicular pressing forces:
- Perpendicular weight: $mg\cos 45^\circ = 20\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$.
- Perpendicular push: $P\sin 45^\circ = 20\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$:
$$R = mg\cos 45^\circ + P\sin 45^\circ$$

Calculate normal reaction:
$$R = 20\sqrt{2} + 20\sqrt{2} = 40\sqrt{2} \approx 56.6\text{ N}$$
The plane supports $56.6\text{ N}$ perpendicular to its face.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves perpendicular to the plane: $R = mg\cos 45^\circ + P\sin 45^\circ$.

$$T = m_B g$$

Equate the tensions:
$$m_B = m_A\sin 30^\circ = 3 \times 0.5 = 1.5\text{ kg}$$
A $1.5\text{ kg}$ counterweight balances the $3\text{ kg}$ mass.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 4: Connected particles over smooth pulley at crest of incline

hints: With $m_B = 4\text{ kg}$, the tension in the string is $T' = 4(10) = 40\text{ N}$.
Block $A$ has downhill gravity of $25\text{ N}$. To balance the $40\text{ N}$ uphill tension, the extra downhill force is $F = 40 - 25 = 15\text{ N}$.
The two string segments pull away from the pulley: one down the slope at $30^\circ$ to horizontal, and one vertically downwards. The angle between them is $90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$.
Use the resultant formula for two equal tensions $T' = 40\text{ N}$ at angle $60^\circ$: $R_P = 2(40)\cos 30^\circ = 40\sqrt{3} \approx 69.3\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the new string tension and extra holding force on block $A$:
- New hanging mass tension: $T' = m_B' g = 4(10) = 40\text{ N}$.
- Equilibrium along the slope for block $A$:
$$\Sigma F_\parallel = T' - mg\sin 30^\circ - F = 0$$
$$40 - 25 - F = 0 \implies F = 15\text{ N} \quad (\text{down the slope})$$

Determine the angle $\phi$ between the two string segments at the pulley:
- The first string segment runs down the slope inclined at $30^\circ$ below the horizontal.
- The second string segment hangs vertically downwards ($90^\circ$ below the horizontal).
$$\phi = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$$

Calculate the resultant force exerted by the string on the pulley:
Both string segments pull with equal tension $T' = 40\text{ N}$ at angle $60^\circ$ to each other:
$$R_P = 2 T' \cos\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right) = 2(40)\cos 30^\circ = 80\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 40\sqrt{3} \approx 69.2820 \approx 69.3\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Balance block $A$ against the heavier load:
- Hanging mass pulls uphill with $T' = 40\text{ N}$.
- Downhill gravity provides $25\text{ N}$, so extra holding force required is:
$$F = 40 - 25 = 15\text{ N} \quad (\text{down the slope})$$

Find geometry of pulley bracket load:
- Angle between the slope string and vertical string is:
$$\phi = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$$

Calculate resultant force on pulley:
- Two $40\text{ N}$ tensions at $60^\circ$ produce a resultant:
$$R_P = 2 \times 40\cos 30^\circ = 40\sqrt{3} \approx 69.3\text{ N}$$
The pulley supports a total clamp load of $69.3\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Forms equilibrium along slope with new tension $T' = 4(10) = 40\text{ N}$: $F + 25 = 40 \implies F = 15\text{ N}$ down the slope.
Identifies that the angle between the two string segments passing over the pulley is $60^\circ$.
Calculates resultant force on pulley: $R_P = 2(40)\cos 30^\circ = 40\sqrt{3} \approx 69.3\text{ N}$.

Find the required tension component:
- The string must supply the missing $14\text{ N}$ of uphill pull:
$$T\cos\theta = 30 - 16 = 14\text{ N}$$

$$T_\perp = T\sin\theta$$

$$R + T\sin\theta - 40 - 12 = 0$$

Express $R$ in terms of $T$ and $\theta$:
$$R = 52 - T\sin\theta$$

$$R = 52 - T\sin\theta$$

hints: When the particle is on the verge of lifting off the smooth plane, the contact force vanishes: $R = 0$.
From part (b), setting $R = 0$ gives $T\sin\theta_c = 52\text{ N}$.
From part (a), $T\cos\theta_c = 14\text{ N}$. Divide the two equations: $\tan\theta_c = \frac{52}{14} = \frac{26}{7} \implies \theta_c \approx 74.9^\circ$.
Find the tension by Pythagoras: $T = \sqrt{14^2 + 52^2} = \sqrt{196 + 2704} = \sqrt{2900} = 10\sqrt{29} \approx 53.9\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the lift-off condition ($R = 0$):
$$R = 52 - T\sin\theta_c = 0 \implies T\sin\theta_c = 52\text{ N}$$

Combine with the parallel equilibrium equation from part (a):
$$T\cos\theta_c = 14\text{ N}$$
$$\tan\theta_c = \frac{T\sin\theta_c}{T\cos\theta_c} = \frac{52}{14} = \frac{26}{7} \approx 3.714286$$
$$\theta_c = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{26}{7}\right) \approx 74.9315^\circ \approx 74.9^\circ$$

Calculate the magnitude of tension $T$:
$$T = \sqrt{(T\cos\theta_c)^2 + (T\sin\theta_c)^2} = \sqrt{14^2 + 52^2} = \sqrt{196 + 2704} = \sqrt{2900} = 10\sqrt{29} \approx 53.8516 \approx 53.9\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify contact loss condition:
- Contact is broken when normal reaction drops to zero:
$$T\sin\theta_c = 52\text{ N}$$
- The string must pull along the slope with:
$$T\cos\theta_c = 14\text{ N}$$

Find the critical angle:
$$\tan\theta_c = \frac{52}{14} = \frac{26}{7} \implies \theta_c \approx 74.9^\circ$$

Compute string tension:
$$T = \sqrt{14^2 + 52^2} = 10\sqrt{29} \approx 53.9\text{ N}$$
At $74.9^\circ$ with $53.9\text{ N}$ of tension, the particle floats weightlessly off the plane.
